$comment: THE QUARANTINE REGISTER. One entry per quarantined test file. It is EMPTY, and
that is the honest state: as of 2026-08-24 this repo has no test it has decided
to stop blocking on. The one measured instability in its history — PGlite files
timing out in beforeAll(open()) at default vitest parallelism, 2026-08-04 — was
answered structurally (60 s hook timeout, then a worker cap, then on 2026-08-24 a
lane split plus a build-once fixture template that removes the 4 s initdb from
the per-file path altogether). Nothing was quarantined and nothing should have
been: a contention symptom is a harness defect, and quarantining it would have
hidden the measurement that fixed it.
An entry here REMOVES its file from the blocking lanes and runs it in the
non-blocking `npm run test:quarantine` lane instead. Entry rules are enforced by
lib/testing/flake/registry.ts and gated by registry.test.ts on every unit run:
an entry needs a named owner (a person, never a team), an entry date, an EXPIRY,
a suspected cause, a form, and a link to the failure evidence. On expiry the gate
goes red — that is what makes quarantine debt rather than amnesty.
GRANULARITY, stated rather than hidden: quarantine here is per FILE, because that
is the unit vitest can exclude from a config without editing the test source. The
`test` field records which test actually flaked so the register stays diagnostic;
it does not narrow what is excluded. Quarantining a file to silence one test is
therefore over-broad, and the ceiling of 5 exists partly to keep that expensive.
An agent must never add an entry here to make a build green (test-harness/
flake-lifecycle). Entries are a human author's decision.
